source_title: van Steenbergen, F.; Lawrence, P.; Mehari Haile, A.; Salman, M.; Faurès, J.-M. (2010). Guidelines on spate irrigation. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 65, Rome.
coverage: Targeted source-purpose screening and relevant passage accounting; not exhaustive main-paper extraction or source sweep.

identity.note: Historical IDs are preserved; citation and artifact title are trust anchors.

targeting_gate.verbatim_anchor:
When new areas are being developed, irrigation engineers and agronomists need 
to determine the potential area that can be irrigated and the capacities of the 
canals that will be needed through estimates of the proportion of annual runoff 
that will be diverted, its distribution in time, and the characteristics of the area to 
be cropped (including soil water-holding capacity).
targeting_gate.rationale: Explicit guidance to determine potential irrigable area when developing new schemes. Main-purpose/planning gate passes without requiring a GIS map.

key_findings: Potential area depends on diverted runoff volume/timing and soil water storage.
Flow-duration/regional hydrology equations are transfer-limited model referrals; engineering tables are not suitability score functions.
Regional hydrology tables3.2–3.4 PDF56–58 retained as design examples, not universal calibration.
holds: 249-page manual only screened and selected spatially relevant passages assessed; not fully swept.
Spate registry wording remains parked; bounded reading does not authorise unpark.
No numeric suitability calibration or dataset binding from these paragraphs.
